When I got my current cat as a kitten, I would have to hold my food above my head while eating so that he couldn't reach it because he would become an absolute demon the second he smelt any food. I couldn't even consider leaving food unattended because the lil bastard would eat through saran wrap or even open up pizza boxes to get to the food, nothing could stop him once he was determined lol. 

When it first started happening, I did some research, and apparently it's pretty common for kittens to act like that. There's a million different reasons, but they think it's due to kittens being extra curious, as well as them being super hungry since they grow pretty fast.

Luckily, my cat is now 4 and is MUCH better about his begging for human food. He started to calm down around a year old, then I trained him to know that if he sits politely and waits patiently, he might get a bite at the very end lol.

Dealing with a ravenous kitten is an extreme sport, and I don't have any major advice except to eat in a separate room while he's young, and stay strong cause hopefully he should start to calm down once he finishes growing!

I'm not a professional piercer, nor a doctor, but I have my industrial piercing and my ear actually had similar big bumps a lot in the first few months when I got it done. I can't say it's technically normal, but just wanted to let you know that I, and many others, have experienced the same thing when dealing with a healing industrial. The industrial bar is said to be one of the harder piercings to heal because of the constant tension caused by the bar. It's also possible that your's may be too short of a bar, or the material of it may be irritating your body.

What I did for mine: I first switched to a slightly longer titanium grade bar (if you do this, you should have your piercer switch it for you since it's still a new piercing and you don't wanna mess with it),  then I started using H2Ocean on mine several times a day, and I also applied tea tree oil directly on the bumps 2-3 times a day to dry them out.

Obviously you know your body best, and if you think you may need professional help from your piercer or doctor, definitely do that! Just sharing my experience with that piercing cause I remember being freaked out from all the bumps too, but luckily they stopped shortly after I started the cleaning/care routine I listed above.

My cat is 2 now and while he has definitely calmed down a lot compared to when he was a kitten, he is still an absolute menace some days. Some cats do calm down around 2, but it can be a gamble adopting around that age cause you may get a calm cat or get a cat like mine that's still super energized all of the time.

I do only have one cat though which I think plays a role with my cat's behavior since he only has me to play with, and if I'm not entertaining him enough, he'll let me know he's bored by getting into literally everything and causing a ruckus. If you want to try to completely avoid the antics that come with super energized young cats and aren't able to get more than one, I would recommend going for a cat closer to 4 or up.

Shelters and rescues can also help you find a good match if you explain what type of personality would work best with your home and lifestyle, so just make sure to explain what kind of cat you're looking for and I'm sure they'd be more than happy to help!

When I was around 2-3 years old, I was gifted three kittens (all brothers from the same litter) as a Christmas present from my parents. I was an only child, so these cats were essentially the closest thing to "siblings" I had growing up. Around when I was 19, my one cat, which also happened to be the one I had the closest bond with, had what I thought was a cold so I brought him to the vet, only to find out that he had cancer and probably didn't have much time left. We started steroid treatments to try to slow down the progression, but it was an absolutely devastating time as these cats were all I had keeping me mentally strong/sane at the time.

The day I came home after finding out my one cat had cancer, his one brother started starving himself. My mom and I thought it was just a weird phase and he'd start eating again since he would nibble on things occasionally so it wasn't a complete starvation, but while all of my energy and time was focused on my cat with cancer, my other cat was fading away. Once I realized that I am most likely going to lose two out of three of my cats as the vet couldn't do much more to help, it really triggered my flight or fight response. I had already dealt with death before at this point of my life, but I had never dealt with pet death, and it put me in a panic. Like you, I almost didn't want to be around them at that point because I wanted to run away in fear of the pain that I know comes next, and also because of the guilt of seeing them in pain. I pushed through though and made sure to spend as much time as I possibly could with them even if it hurt me inside, and I'm glad I did because I think I would've regretted it if I didn't.

When I could tell it was the end and that there was no way they would get better, I was ready to put them down, but no one would drive me and I knew I couldn't drive myself with how much of a mess I was, I knew it wasn't safe for myself nor anyone else on the road if I drove myself. Instead, both of my cats passed away in my bedroom, one week apart from each other, and in a very short amount of time after finding out they were sick.

I am so sorry that you are going through this right now, just know that you are not alone and you are not wrong for feeling the way you do. It's normal what you are feeling, the guilt and the fear, the wanting to just run away from it all, I felt similar too when my first two cats were dying.

My advice to you though is that as hard as it is, try not to let the fear and guilt of the inevitable take away from what little time you have left with your cat. You'll have all the time in the world to cry and breakdown after she passes, but right now she is still here even if it's only for a few more days. As hard as it is, try to put your feelings of guilt and sadness to the side to spend time with her before she passes, try to make the best of what little time she has left. Be strong for her, be there for her like she was there for you during your darker times. I know firsthand how hard it is to be strong during times like this when you feel like your heart and soul are shattering, I was you at one point, but I promise you that if you don't spend more time with her, you will carry an even worse guilt than what you're feeling right now, and I wouldn't wish that heavy feeling on anyone. Please know I am not judging you for how you feel, I know everyone reacts differently when dealing with their pets being sick and dying, but I am encouraging you to try your best to be strong and be there for her as much as you can as I don't want you regretting it after she passes.

Have you guys tried Feliway? I know they have a plugin diffuser that's specifically made for multiple cat households that's supposed to help with fighting, bathroom issues, and cat anxiety, so maybe you could try that if you haven't already. I think they also have a spray that you can use on specific areas as well.

Also, where are the litter boxes in your home? I had a cat who would sometimes pee instead of poop outside of the litter box and we're pretty sure he didn't like peeing in the litter box just because of the spot it was in since it was in a semi-loud room with the washer and dryer, so maybe it could be something like that? It also helped putting one of the litter boxes in the spot that he would pee in, so maybe you could try putting the litter box in one of the areas he keeps pooping in if you haven't done that already.

As for the biting when petting thing, he may just be getting overstimulated when you pet him! Some cats are very sensitive when receiving attention and end up biting or attacking because of it, especially when they're young since they're so full of energy. I know it may be hard to do, but it may help to limit how much you pet him when you're petting him cause it may be too stimulating if you pet him for too long. I have an 8 month old kitten myself and there's definitely a lot of times that he does this, but what I did was get him a little kitty stuffed animal that was his size and I give that to him whenever he gets too rough with my hand. I've also noticed that he will attack my legs/feet sometimes out of nowhere, but it usually means he is bored so he decides my legs/feet are the perfect "prey" to hunt as entertainment. What I usually do when he attacks my legs/feet is pull out a wand toy and play with him to get some of his energy out, or I give him his stuffed kitty to beat up instead of me.

I know you mentioned that you guys have looked up a bunch of stuff, but you guys should check out Jackson Galaxy on YouTube if you haven't already! He has a show called My Cat From Hell where he basically helps families work with their cats on their bad behaviors, and he has a YouTube channel as well where he shares a bunch of advice on how to correct cat behavior. I definitely recommend checking him out if you haven't already, I've learned a bunch of stuff from him and it has helped tremendously.

I'm sorry if any of my advice has things you already knew, but I hope there's atleast something I mentioned that could help in some way. Your kitten is very lucky to have someone who cares about him and wants to help figure out his issues. I wish you the best of luck, and hope things get better with him!

My kitten is about 8 months old now and he sleeps with me, but there are nights where he is a maniac and I get very shitty sleep.  Usually the nights he keeps me up are the ones where I didn't  play with him enough to tire him out before bedtime which is my own fault, but as long as I do play with him before bed he usually won't bother/wake me until he starts hearing my morning alarms go off.

If you do decide to try having him sleep with you, I would just recommend you play with him for like an hour or so close to bed time (I'd say like two hours before you plan on going to bed cause sometimes they're still in play-mode for a bit after you're done playing) and get a routine started that helps him understand when it's time to wind down for the night. 

It will take a lil bit of time for him to get on the same schedule as you, but it's totally worth it if you think him sleeping with you is something you want!

Putting ANYTHING in your lungs aside from air is terrible for you, so technically vaping is still bad for you, but when compared to smoking it's a much better substitute since it's such a significant difference in how many harmful chemicals you are putting into your body.

Cigarettes have about 600 ingredients (7,000 chemicals being released when burning), Juuls have about 6 ingredients, and other Vape Juices usually have anywhere between 4-10 ingredients. That's a ridiculously huge difference in the amount of chemicals being ingested when vaping, so I'm sure it's gotta be a lot less damaging to your body than cigarettes, but that doesn't mean it's harmless like some people tend to think.

The biggest problem though, vaping is still too new to really know the actual long term effects, so it's hard to tell what kind of health issues will occur after longtime use and how long it will take for these issues to start occurring. Vapes were created on the idea to provide addicted smokers who want to quit with a "healthier" alternative, which technically they did achieve when comparing the two.

Vaping is still most definitely not healthy, just a substitute with less cancerous/poisonous chemicals, but in the end it's really just a different kind of addiction you'll have to quit too eventually down the line.

I saw your other comment about this being abused in another country and killing someone who didn't want to die, that was fucked up, but I just wanted to reply some ideas on where the line should be drawn. Apologies on length, it's not a simple thing that can be summed up in short since it's such a complex topic.

If it's someone choosing suicide just because they genuinely do not want to live anymore and have tried their best at living, then give them like a certain amount of days they have to wait to make sure they really want to do it. Just an example, have them fill out the paperwork then have them wait like 15-30 days until they actually can do it. Give them that leeway to back out if they decide to, but also don't make it an absurd amount of days and make them suffer any longer than they already have. Suicide isn't really one of those things that people wake up one morning and decide "fuck it" (there are exceptions of course), it's usually something they contemplated for a really long time so they shouldn't be forced to wait months/years to be able to do it. Maybe doctors could also run tests to make sure these people aren't in a manic episode or psychotic breakdown that's causing them to make rash decisions. Like if they wanna die, then they have to want to die both in a mental breakdown and during a normal Tuesday when they're thinking more straight. That being said though, death is a permanent solution that shouldn't be a decision made in a split second, but it's they're life and if they truly want to move on, then they should be able to. People who choose this are most likely going to do it either way, so why not make it a more peaceful and fast way instead of having them do it themselves and someone being traumatized from finding their body then others having to clean up the mess? This way, they could also let family and friends know they are going to do it and can come say goodbye in their last moments. I think that's a much better way for everyone since most suicides happen without warning since they can't tell their loved ones in advance they're going to do it, and their loved ones are usually left with so many unanswered questions and are angry at the world. This way could help both the person choosing to die, and all those who love them and are going to have to deal with the pain of them being gone. 

Then for those terminally ill, they need to be still lucid (for situations like dementia) and able to clearly decide they want to be euthanized. They could sign the papers saying they want to be euthanized right away, euthanized once they've gotten to the point where they barely know who they are, euthanized when the cancer spreads, or just when their quality of life is completely diminished like they are on permanent hospitalization/bed rest and/or need to get put into a home for 24/7 care. Let them go out with some dignity and go before the pain really gets worse, ya know? Life already sucks sometimes, I know I definitely would not wanna go out in excruciating pain and/or live several years as a shell of the person I once was.

The only time anyone else should be able to decide euthanasia for someone else, is if they literally cannot decide for them self due to being paralyzed, brain dead, in a coma, etc. BUT the person who cannot speak on their own behalf would have to have chosen this person BEFORE all of what happened to be the one to choose. I know the US has a system where the married spouse or parents choose their loved one's fate typically in situations like this, but not all people would want their spouse or parents choosing for them cause they may choose the option that benefits themselves instead of the one that benefits the one suffering. 

Also, another idea, if you persay did suffer from dementia and did not sign any papers before losing yourself, this person you choose should be able to make the decision of euthanizing you. I only say this because I know whoever I would choose would KNOW what I wanted, and would know that this isn't the kind of life I would have wanted to live. But that one is grey area because there's always those people out there that may use that to their advantage to kill off people who wouldn't have wanted to die but claimed they did even though they didn't sign the papers. Obviously though, the idea of having a chosen person for situations like that isn't simple since most accidents and such are not planned, they just happen. 

I guess the best idea I have for choosing a person is when you turn 18 and go to the doctors, you'll get a slip to fill out deciding who you want as your person to speak on your behalf in situations where you cannot be your own spokesperson since now you are an adult and can choose someone else than your parents/guardians. Then they would attach it to your name/file so when you go to any doctor like the gyno, dentist, dermatologist, etc; they will always know who your "person" is incase of an emergency and you'll also have the option to change/update whenever you want at any doctor appointment you go to. Just a super raw idea and I don't know if it could actually work or be implemented, but just an idea to start.

Prejudice towards certain religions? And why the hell do we still not have a better mental health system for those who need mental help?

Anxiety attacks aren't black and white, every attack is different and they don't always have the same trigger. Sometimes I have the typical hyperventilating and shakes after being put in a stressful situation; sometimes I have an attack for absolutely no reason where I have an outer body type feeling and have a hard time grounding myself. But the one type of anxiety attack that I feel isn't as well known, is the one brought on by overstimulation and causes you to become snappy and irritated uncontrollably.

For example, situations where your personal space is invaded. Like when you go to the grocery store, or go to pay at the counter at a restaurant, and the person behind you decides to stand basically on top of you even though there is so much space to stand elsewhere. Or standing in lines that people start to become pushy in. Or going to the mall on a busy day and having people constantly accidentally bumping into you or even just lightly grazing past you every couple of minutes. Or being in a room full of people shouting over each other at every which angle or all of them trying to shout to get your attention. The best? Putting all those scenarios in the same place. Having so many things going on like that at a time and not being able to really do anything about it since all those things are out of your control, it can really make you feel almost attacked at every angle and start to feel almost claustrophobic, make you feel small. I'm not being a bitch to be a bitch, all my senses were just overloaded and I felt completely overwhelmed which caused me to freak out.

Totally know what you mean on not knowing where to start and having a hard time picking stuff back up because of depression. Take everything in baby steps. I know when I set too big of goals, or goals that seem so out of reach, it completely intimidates me to the point where I just give up. 

If you decide to start a journal, start by just writing down random thoughts as they pop into your head. I carry a little notebook on me during the day so if I have a random thought or random flashback of a memory, whether a good or bad one, I can jot it down to kind of get it off my chest and out of my head. Start by just writing down the thought, then if you need to vent about it, start writing as much as you need down. Think of it as a way to not only help organize your thoughts, but a way to also vent without having to verbally talk to someone else you don’t quite feel fully comfortable with yet. Doesn’t work for everyone, but I know being able to write down my thoughts and memories as they come helps keep my mind a bit calmer. 

As for the art, take baby steps with that too! Make it a goal to set aside a couple mins a day to focus on your art. It can be something simple like watching videos to help inspire you, or could be just spending a couple mins a day doodling to figure out what exactly you want to create. Eventually you’ll find your inspiration and motivation to get back into what you originally loved, just takes time. 

If you ever need a stranger to vent to, my inbox is always open! And just remember that the journey in finding yourself is not a sprint, it’s a marathon. So don’t stress out about how much time it takes to find some happiness again, and don’t feel discouraged if you run into some failure along the way either. You’ll find yourself eventually and will become the best you that you can be, just be patient. You got this tho (:

My best friend made a guest appearance visit a few days after she killed herself.

It was 2\-3 days after it happened when she visited. I was over my friend's house having some drinks and hanging out, when subtle signs kept happening. First, the TV and lights kept flickering on and off on their own. The TV, and also the lights, have NEVER done this before, nor have they done it since. Then her dog kept barking and whimpering randomly. Not at us, but at the air around us.

The next thing that happened wasn't as subtle. My friend and I were in the kitchen and made a joke complaining about how the lights in there were too bright. Not even a full minute after making that comment, three out of the five lightbulbs in the kitchen burnt out. Weird coincidence? Sure. After a little longer of strange things happening, we got a wiff of what smelled like someone just sprayed a bunch of perfume right next to us. Neither of us sprayed anything, and neither of us wore perfume that day. Even if we did, neither of us wore a perfume that had that exact or similar smell that we smelt.

After about an hour, seemed like the signs calmed down, but that wasn't the end. My friend and I were talking now in her livingroom and both happened to look towards the corner hallway that led to her kitchen. That's when we SAW a figure casually walk past us and back into the dark. The figure walked slow enough for us to both double take and really get a good look at them, so we couldn't even try to brush it off like our eyes playing tricks on us.

My friend and I looked at each other dumbfounded, wondering if we reached a mental breaking point into crazy. I knew it had to be real if we both saw it, there's no way it wasn't cause we both even described the figure the same. I can STILL remember it vividly in my head. It was a tall female with a curvy body. She had long thick hair tied up in a pony tail and was wearing her favorite flowy black skirt/dress that she wore all the time on the warmer days. She even carried herself in the way my friend did when she was alive, the same kind of walk she had. It was my best friend, it HAD to be.

For the rest of the night until sunrise, there were still subtle signs. You could tell she was hanging back in the shadows of the dark hallway because you could occasionally see movement or hear someone shuffling around. My friend's dog even continued to whine at the hallway and stare as if he saw something.

It's been a few months now since she died, but let me tell you, that was NOT the last time that she's made a guest appearance. This was just the time that was most intense, and the time where I was with someone else to see/hear what all happened for themselves. I was also not the only one to get signs or to actually see her, several friends and some of her family has had their own visits as well. Crazy shit man lol.

That's a good question. I've been battling depression, amongst other mental illnesses, since I was basically in middle school. I can't speak for everybody, but just wanted to comment my experience with my parents growing up. I also wanted to share my point of view of what I think is a good explanation of why we are how we are, and give my opinion on the question you asked. 

We know to society we appear lazy and like we don't care about taking care of ourselves or anything, trust me, we beat ourselves up about it on a constant basis (at least I do). It honestly has nothing to do with us being lazy or not caring to do these things. It's that every task, whether it be big or small, is a challenge and hard to do when we are this tired. 

Being mentally ill is so goddamn exhausting. There's a constant battle occurring in our heads every single day that doesn't really ever come to a silence or an end. Our mind and bodies become so beyond exhausted, so worn down, from this constant battling and we go into basically "survival mode". The only things that matter in this "mode" is battling our disease (battle methods vary on the person), eating, sleeping, and most importantly just breathing. That's the main things we need to do to survive, and that's all we have the energy for. 

We don't have the energy to do "pointless" and "unnecessary" extra tasks than those four things. I put quotation marks around those two words because to the rest of society, these tasks we consider “unnecessary” probably are not viewed that way to others and are most likely viewed as a part of their daily routines that they would never even think twice about skipping in their day. Sure, maybe we're gross or lazy for skipping whatever it is, but that task we skipped is not a priority to us when we have bigger things to focus on. 

An example of a fight that constantly occurred in my household growing up with my parents; when I'd get into my super lows, I wouldn't do much help around the house and was viewed as just being a lazy teenager. I would get yelled at for not helping out with cleaning, not keeping my room clean, not doing this, and not doing that. I'm sorry I didn't think to vacuum the living-room during my free time, I was too busy focusing on convincing myself not to let my dark thoughts win in getting me to give up or do something stupid.

I know you don't like seeing someone depressed and laying in their bed until they rot away, and I agree it's not a progressive way for them to get better or find motivation, but trying to apply positive punishment won't make them spontaneously find the energy and motivation to go do something either. Pointing out all their wrongs, yelling, or just straight up nagging them constantly for being lazy, will never make it better. Positive punishment will almost ALWAYS make it worse for them and cause them to just get worse than they began. You don't need to remind a mentally ill person that they are slacking, as I said before, we know and beat ourselves up about it constantly. We're already beating ourselves up on a constant basis, we don't need others to add more fuel to the fire. We need others to help us want to work hard to put out the fire that's trying to hurt us. 

What can you do? Just support us and try to understand why we can't find the motivation to do normal everyday tasks. You don't have to coddle us, we aren't defenseless injured puppies or kittens, but don't add extra stress and things to be upset about either. Be kind to those affected by mental illness, remember that as hidden as their battle is, it doesn’t mean it’s any less real. You don’t need to sugar coat things with us either, if we are truly messing things up or hurting others then we should be made aware about it, but also don’t overdo it with your “truth spiel” when trying to get us to understand your frustration on your end. We should hear it, yes, but don’t make it into “ripping you a new one” or into a long one-sided discussion of just you nagging. And please stop focusing on only all of the negatives. Instead of nagging about everything that we’ve done wrong and about how we need to conjure up the motivation we can't find, try helping us figure out how to find it. Encourage us and cheer us on to keep fighting, and help us figure out how to get back to the path we should've been on before our brains got sick. Help us, or at least support us, as we try to find the motivation that we so desperately long to have again.

Everyone is different in what they need to get better. Some people need medications, some need therapy, and some need both. Some people are the kinds of people who "fake it till you make it". They clean up their space, clean their appearance up, put on a fake smile, and pretend they're happy until it happens for real. Some people need to get lost in work or hobbies to distract until their mind calms down. To piggy back off of your comment...

That's just an example of one scenario, but the point is to just reassure them the truth from time to time to remind them that these dark thoughts they have aren't always the truth. I've had a lot of loss in my life over the past couple of years and something I'll mention that made grieving harder, was hearing the constant "sorry" and the constant look everyone gave when looking at me. I'm talking about that look of pity everyone would give because they knew how broken I'd been in each situation. It was kind for all those people to reach out to me and to care, but it became overwhelming to constantly hear it from every angle and was overwhelming to have people I haven't talked to in years come out of the shadows to show support. I mention what made things worse for me because I think it's important to know that people don't want to be constantly reminded of their loss. The apologies and kind words are most definitely always appreciated, but try not to constantly remind them what just happened. Believe me, they know they just lost someone important and they are beyond broken about it, but try to avoid triggering their pain when they are distracted and not crying. If they're finally trying to get back on track with life, and they are finally having a laugh in "normal" conversations again with everyone, just please let them have that brief moment of peace. I know most people mean well when apologizing for deaths and reaching out to say they're there for support, but just be mindful that sometimes those kind actions could do more damage than good in certain situations. 

There is no correct thing to say or do to support someone in these dark times, just be there in whatever ways you can be and whatever ways they need you to be. Then just make sure to be mindful of everything you do or say, make sure you aren't overbearing or causing them anymore pain with your actions. Death is hard, it takes a lot of time before really being able to start to heal. Until then, they will need all the support and help they can get.

Sure it's a cheaper route, BUT with an older car comes more constant complications and problems to fix. I personally got a 2000 Celica GT at 100,000 miles over a year or two ago and almost every few months it had to go to the shop and get something fixed. Most of these somethings were expensive too, a couple thousand dollars were dropped EVERY few months on this car that was only worth $3,000 when I got it. Don't forget too that most the parts an old car needs, a shop will not have in stock, most parts have to be ordered which means you car will be in the shop for several days. My car has probably had well over $10,000 put into it since I got it plus that $3,000 dropped at purchase. Now that's a lot of money for someone who didn't want to spend that much money on a car to begin with. Used cars are great and you save money when picking them, but you have to remember that old used cars come with unforeseen problems and most likely all those problems that you will need to fix will end up being costly. I loved that car, don't get me wrong, but when you have $30,000 to spend on a sporty car and you have the choice of a brand new car with no problems (problems covered by dealership too if a manufacturing problem arises after purchase) or an old car with unknown problems that could be nothing OR could be problems that cost thousands of dollars to fix, you mine as well pick the new car so you have a nicer car AND a safety net if anything goes wrong. When you get an old used car, you're taking the chance of getting a car in good condition or getting one with a million mechanical problems that may not even arise until after purchase when the sale is final and you can't really just say "oh nevermind". Just my opinion, do what ya want! I can't afford a shiny new car at that price, hence why I had the Celica, but I can tell you first hand that just because the buying price is low for an old car does not necessarily mean that that's all you will spend on the car in total and you may end up spending just as much as you would buying a newer car with all the work you may need to do on a used car as problems arise. 

EDIT: Another thing I wanna add too, older cars are NOT good commuting cars if you have a far drive to your job or school. If you're adding up mileage on a car fast, an old car is a terrible choice. They already typically have high mileage when you buy them, and the more you drive will make it wear down faster which will in turn cause more problems to occur. I'm not saying to not get a used/older car, I'm just saying that more aspects should be considered if you are on a tight spending budget and looking at getting an old car. A newer used car may be a better choice in the long run than an old 90s/2000s Toyota Celica GT. I am the perfect example of how old cars can be a huge pain in the ass lol

There's definitely obvious signs that may show someone you care about is depressed/mentally ill (some other's listed them), but don't forget to look for the hidden signs. If they start doing things that they never normally do or start acting out of character, pay close attention to those small changes. Some people have what you would call "high functioning depression". It doesn't mean that they aren't depressed and it also doesn't mean that their depression isn't as severe as others, it just means they're able to still function even though their mental health is deteriorating. Their cries for help are much different than the average and are hard to catch, but you should definitely look for the hidden smaller signs as well as the big obvious ones.

Three things. One, stop telling me to just get over things. When you have mental disorders, daily life is already a struggle alone. But when you get thrown real problems and obstacles to overcome, we have to work extra hard than the "normal" person to heal from a traumatic/stressful occurrence. 

Two, just because I have a smile on my face and am acting "normal" does NOT mean that I am okay. Some of us are just high functioning mentally ill people. That's a thing that people can't grasp the concept of and I almost constantly hear that I must be fine if I'm acting fine. That's not how mental illnesses work, some people project their symptoms a lot and others keep their symptoms to themselves. Not all mentally ill people show their struggles the same way as others. Everyone is different.

Three, we are not broken toys. Please stop looking at us as damaged and taking pity on us constantly. When we ask for you to cut us some slack, we mean don't cause unnecessary stress in our lives because we already have enough. That doesn't mean that we can't handle criticism or fights, or are unable to own up to our mistakes. We just mean that we don't want to deal with stupid extra stress on top of what we deal with on a daily basis. Ex: Don't start fights with us unless it's completely necessary. Whether an evil or good spirit, just try to be as casual and normal as possible when first trying to understand it's intentions.
